newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai c/a deficit steady, exports sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Thai c/a deficit steady, exports sluggish.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Thursday announced a moderate current account deficit for September, but said the country's sluggish exports showed no signs of recovery.
The central bank released monthly economic indicators showing that the September current account deficit widened slightly to 30.5 billion baht ($1.22 billion) from 29.3 billion in August.
It said exports declined to 112.5 billion baht in September, a 9.3 percent drop from the same period last year.
The BOT said exports in the first nine months of 1996 rose only 0.9 percent, compared to more than 20 percent the same period last year.
But it said the September trade deficit narrowed to 25 billion baht from 36.8 billion in August because imports declined to 137.5 billion baht from 154.5 billion baht in August.
Kleo-thong Hetrakul, a central bank spokeswoman, said that despite the lower exports, the bank projected the gross domestic product in 1996 to grow by nearly 7.0 percent.
"Despite the low export growth, the GDP for all of 1996 will not be lower than six percent but not higher than seven percent. I expect it to be close to seven percent," she said.
She also said the current account deficit should stand near the 1995 level of 8.1 percent of GDP in 1996.

The BOT said outstanding bank credit growth, excluding imported off-shore funds, continued a downward trend that began late last year and increased 14.2 percent year-on-year in October, compared with 15.6 percent in September.
But it said Thailand's private investment index posted an 8.3 percent year-on-year growth in September, up from 8.0 percent in August.
